## Why support matters more than network size


A bigger warmup network doesn't fix a broken setup. If your SPF record doesn't include the service you send from, your DKIM key isn't published, or your DMARC policy is misconfigured, mailbox providers can still filter your emails, whatever the size of the network warming them up.


That's why every Mailwarm customer gets an account manager. They help you set up your account, check and configure your[SPF, DKIM and DMARC records](https://www.mailwarm.com/free-email-deliverability-tools) , connect your inboxes and plan your ramp-up. Then they stay with you: deliverability expert calls are included on every plan, so when something changes in your sending, someone who already knows your setup is there to help.


Warmup is the part that runs automatically. The expertise around it is what keeps you in the inbox, and it's what we've been doing since 2020.

## Why teams look for a Warmy alternative


### 1.


Cost as you add inboxes


Price is the most repeated complaint in reviews. Plans start at $49 a month, and reviewers describe the service as "not cheap", especially as a team adds mailboxes.


### 2.


Limited control over warmup settings


Several reviewers wanted more customization of warmup behavior and a dashboard with more depth than the default view.


### 3.


Provider and reliability issues


A few reviewers reported that warming Gmail accounts worked less well than expected, or that warmup stopped running for a period before it was noticed.

## Warmy alternative: frequently asked questions


How much does Warmy.io cost?


Warmy's pricing page lists plans starting from $49 a month, with a 7-day free trial that needs no credit card. Higher plans add more mailboxes and features, and a Custom plan includes a dedicated success manager. Prices were checked in October 2026, so confirm the current figures on Warmy's own pricing page before you decide.


What are people saying about Warmy.io in reviews?


Warmy holds a 4.8 out of 5 rating from 55 reviews on Capterra. The most common complaints are price, limited control over warmup settings, and a few reports of Gmail warmup or reliability problems. For comparison, Mailwarm is rated 4.9 out of 5 on Capterra, with 5.0 for customer service. Ratings checked October 2026.


What is the best email warmer?


The best email warmer is the one that gets your setup right, not the one with the biggest network. Warmup only works when SPF, DKIM and DMARC are configured correctly and your domain reputation is healthy. That's why Mailwarm pairs automated warmup with people: every customer gets an account manager who helps set up DNS, authentication fix tools, and deliverability expert calls on every plan.


Which is better, Warmy or Mailwarm?


It depends on what is holding your deliverability back. Most inbox placement problems come from setup: SPF, DKIM and DMARC records, domain reputation and how fast sending ramps up. That's where Mailwarm is the stronger choice, because every customer gets an account manager who fixes the setup with them and deliverability expert calls on every plan. Warmy is built for teams that want a very large network and seed testing and prefer to handle their setup themselves.


Does a bigger warmup network mean better deliverability?


Not on its own. A larger network gives a warmup tool more inboxes to interact with, but it can't make up for a missing DKIM signature, an SPF record that doesn't include your sending service, or a domain with a poor reputation. Those are the issues that decide where your emails land. Mailwarm gets them right with you first, then runs warmup across 50,000+ aged real inboxes.


Does Mailwarm help me set up SPF, DKIM and DMARC?


Yes. Every Mailwarm customer gets an account manager who checks your SPF, DKIM and DMARC records, helps you add or fix them with your DNS provider, and confirms they pass. Most deliverability problems start with authentication, so it's the first thing we look at.


How do I switch from Warmy to Mailwarm?


Book your onboarding call first. Your account manager reviews your current setup, including SPF, DKIM and DMARC, then helps you connect the same inboxes and start a gradual ramp-up. Once Mailwarm is running, pause warmup in Warmy so the two tools don't double your daily volume.


Does Mailwarm support the same email providers as Warmy?


Mailwarm supports Gmail and Google Workspace, Outlook and Microsoft 365, Yahoo and Zoho, plus SMTP providers including SendGrid, Mailgun, Amazon SES, Postmark and custom SMTP. Warmy lists support for more than 140 ESPs, so if you send through a marketing platform such as Klaviyo, check that your setup is covered before switching.
